$comment: The machine-readable half of docs/cloud-frames.md: the rules every
implementation of the cloud verb layer must agree on. Edit THIS file,
then run `python3 frameos/tools/generate_cloud_contract.py` — it writes
the tables for the Linux runtime (Nim), the ESP32 firmware (C), the
cloud (TS) and the SPA (TS). docs/cloud-frames-fixtures.json holds the
conformance cases all three verb-layer implementations run.
Rule language (validators are ~100 lines per language, see
frameos/src/frameos/cloud/contract.nim, embedded/esp32/main/
fos_cloud_contract.c, cloud/apps/auth-web/src/lib/cloud-frames-contract.ts):
{type: bool}
{type: int, min?, max?, enum?}              integers only
{type: number, min?, max?}                  int or float
{type: string, minLen?, maxLen?, enum?, format?}
format: iana_zone | html_hex_color | gpio_label
{type: object, keys: {name: rule}, required?: [], minKeys?, open?}
unknown keys refuse the value unless open
{type: array, items: rule, maxItems?}
{type: map, values: rule, maxEntries?, keyMinLen?, keyMaxLen?}
{type: null}
{anyOf: [rule, ...]}
Checks the language cannot express are listed under `extraChecks` and
implemented by hand in every validator.
Per setting: `profiles` names who accepts the key. `since` is the first
firmware version that does (null = every version; the provider gates a
push on the frame's reported frameos_version because a device refuses the
WHOLE verb on a key it does not know). `rule` inside a profile overrides
the top-level rule for that profile. `restart` = applying it restarts the
runtime (Linux) or reboots the chip (ESP32). `companion` = only valid next
to that other key in the same push.
`parity` (2026-09-06): a key accepted by one profile only MUST carry
`parity: {only, why}` naming the plane and the reason the other cannot
take it; a key both accept must not. The generator refuses the file
otherwise, so no new key ships single-plane silently. Each key that
goes both-planes deletes its parity entry; the count of entries IS the
measured parity gap (docs/convergence-todo.md item 6).

timezone_data.$comment: The zone's tzdata slice for a chip without a tz database; command payload only, never a stored setting. null = fetch it yourself.

parity.why: The POSIX TZ string for the chip's libc; the Pi has tzdata and takes `timezone` alone.

auto_update.$comment: The daily self-update channel. `stable` (default): once a day the device checks ITS OWN signed release channel — a frame with a self-hosted backend follows the release that backend runs (the backend deploys its own version, so a frame never climbs past it); a cloud-managed or standalone Pi asks GitHub, an ESP32 its provider's manifest relay — and installs the latest release once it has been the latest for 24 h — a fix published within a day resets the clock, so the release it fixes is never installed. `latest`: install every release as soon as it is published. `off`: never check. A provider can only pick the channel, never name what gets installed; the manual paths (the admin panel's Upgrade button, the console's `ota`, notify_update_available) stay open either way.

parity.why: The Pi runtime flips the framebuffer in pixie; the ESP32 render path has rotate only, no flip stage (fos_http.c reports "").

error_behavior.$comment: The frontend/backend spelling; the runtime maps it onto errorBehavior in frame.json.

parity.why: The Pi runtime's scene-error retry policy (safe mode, retry windows); the ESP32 restarts the scene on an error and has no such state machine.

control_code.$comment: The runtime's controlCode shape: a bool, numbers and #rrggbb colours — not the SPA form's string spellings.

parity.why: Renders the local-presence pairing code overlay on the Pi; the ESP32 has no on-device pairing UI (its console prints what it needs).

metrics_interval.$comment: 0 disables the sampler; anything else is a period in seconds.

parity.why: The Pi runtime pushes metrics on its own timer; the ESP32 pushes them on its render cadence and reports a fixed 60 (fos_http.c).

max_http_response_bytes.$comment: A per-request memory bound. The Linux ceiling is the runtime's own default (64 MiB) so a push can only lower it; the chip takes 1 KiB up.

save_assets.$comment: One switch, or a per-app-keyword map of switches.

parity.why: Caches downloaded images into the Pi's assets directory; the ESP32 has no writable assets cache beyond the optional SD card.

timezone_updater.$comment: enabled/hour only: the download URL is never a provider's to set.

parity.why: A Pi cron/systemd timer refreshing tzdata; the ESP32 receives its zone as timezone_data instead.

palette.$comment: frame.json's palette: #rrggbb colours plus optional display name and per-colour names. An empty colour list hands the panel back its built-in palette.
extraChecks: colorNames, when present, has exactly as many entries as colors

parity.why: Custom dithering palette for the Pi renderer; ESP32 panels dither to their driver's fixed palette.

device_config.$comment: STRICTLY the partial-refresh policy; the rest of deviceConfig is hardware wiring and stays the device's own (the persist path patches).

parity.why: Pi driver knobs (partial refresh, VCOM, …); on the ESP32 the panel table carries them per board.

gpio_buttons.$comment: [{pin, label}] — the whole list, replaced; an empty list unbinds every button. The chip's table is smaller, and the firmware refuses (invalid_settings) any pin that is an SPI flash / PSRAM pad or already a driver's on that chip (fos_config_gpio_pin_reserved): the range here is chip-agnostic, the reservation is not.

parity.why: ESP32 power management; a Pi has no deep sleep.
ESP32 power management; a Pi has no deep sleep or battery sense.

wake_check_seconds.$comment: 0 = only wake to render; the firmware clamps 1..59 up to 60 (sub-minute check-ins drain a battery for nothing).

parity.why: ESP32 deep-sleep wake cadence; a Pi never sleeps.

battery_pin.$comment: ADC GPIO; -1 = no battery sense. Read at boot. The firmware refuses (invalid_settings) an SPI flash / PSRAM pad or a driver-claimed pin for its chip.

parity.why: ESP32 ADC battery sense; a Pi has no ADC.
ESP32 ADC battery sense; a Pi has no ADC.

battery_enable_pin.$comment: GPIO driven high to switch the divider on while sampling (reTerminal E1004: 21); -1 = always on. Same reserved-pin refusal as battery_pin.

parity.why: ESP32 ADC battery sense; a Pi has no ADC.

formats.gpio_label: 1..32 characters after trimming whitespace, no ':' and no newline

errors.$comment: The tokens every implementation answers with. Per-verb tokens beyond these are in docs/cloud-frames.md.
errors.backend_managed: a device whose content a self-hosted backend owns refuses every `content` verb with this

limits.$comment: Wire caps, per profile where the small device differs.
